newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends shade lower after early big drop.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends shade lower after early big drop.

text.p: The South Korean won closed slightly lower on Wednesday after much of the early decline was offset by late dollar selling sparked by a senior central bank official's remarks, dealers said.
The Bank of Korea official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters the won was seen at an appropriate level.
"The remarks sent a signal that the bank would not let the dollar exceed the 900 won level," said a foreign bank dealer.
The won ended at 894.30, against Tuesday's close of 894.00. It rose to 894.50 at opening on the Japanese yen's decline against the U.S. dollar, and ranged between 893.60 and 896.50.
Dealers said the market was seen still heavy with dollars and that a significant rise of the dollar could be swiftly followed by increased dollar selling.
"Banks are now steadily reducing their dollar positions on expectations the current range would be kept for the time being," said a domestic bank dealer.
He forecast an 893-897 range for Thursday, while the foreign bank dealer put the range at between 893.00 and 894.50.
Dealers expected the won's base mid-rate to be pegged at 895.20 on Thursday, compared with 894.20 on Wednesday.
